title: Compute spin‑wave damping/frequency coefficients and critical correlation time
action: Compute the coefficients A₁, A₂, A₃ using the explicit formulas above. Use ξ = 1/(1+α²). For each (α,D) pair on a grid with α ∈ [0, 2] (at least 20 points) and D ∈ [−2, 2] (at least 20 points) and fixed μ=0.9, τ=1, evaluate A₁, A₂, A₃. Also compute τ_c from its formula; if denominator is zero or τ_c<0 set to NaN. Write the results to /app/outputs/stability_output.csv.
description: A table containing the analytically evaluated coefficients that determine spin‑wave stability. The grid shows the dependence on damping and noise, revealing the region where damped solutions exist (A1>0) and the critical correlation time where compensation occurs.
output_schema: CSV with columns: alpha, D, A1, A2, A3, tau_c. Each row corresponds to one (α, D) point on the grid. tau_c can be NaN. All numeric values are floating-point.

title: Solve correlation function ODE for C₁₂(s)
action: Form the G matrix from the previously computed A₁, A₂, A₃ for the parameters μ=0.9, α=0.005, D=0.1, τ=1. Extract the linear coupling tensor L from Λ (Λ_{ik}(ψ) = Σ_p L_{ikp} ψ_p) and construct the 9×9 matrix M with M_{ij,pq} = Σ_k L_{ikp} L_{jkq}. Assemble the ODE system for the 9 components C_{ij} as: d C_{ij} / ds = Σ_k G_{ik} C_{kj} + D e^{-s/τ} Σ_{p,q} M_{ij,pq} C_{pq}. Set initial condition C_{ij}(0) = 1.0 for all i,j. Numerically integrate from s=0 to s=10 using a dense output at spacing 0.1. Extract the component C₁₂(s) and write to /app/outputs/correlation_C12.csv.
description: The time evolution of the spin‑spin correlation component C₁₂(s) obtained by numerically integrating the closed deterministic ODE derived from the joint probability approach. This curve demonstrates the oscillatory damping behaviour influenced by the finite noise correlation time.
output_schema: CSV with columns: s, C12. s ranges from 0 to 10 in steps of 0.1. C12 is a floating‑point number.
